title: fix(app-shell): the by-name object scope leaves a failed read unanswered, not missing (objectui#13009)
body:
Fixes #13009
Clause-②: no

## What

`MetadataProvider`'s by-name object scope (`fetchScopeName`) used to record every `null` from `getItem` as `missing`, and `getItem` answers `null` for a failed read too. So a transient 5xx or a network drop read as "this deployment has no such object" for the session, and `useObjectPresence` answered `absent` (the bell's Activity feed read as unavailable) where its contract says an error reads `unknown`.

- A private `readItem(type, name)` now carries the shared by-name read (dedup, cache, normalization) and answers `{ item, failed }`. `failed` is `true` only when no answer was obtained; a thrown `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (the contract code, read with the existing `isMetaItemAbsentError` from `@object-ui/data-objectstack`) and a read that resolves with no document are answers (`failed: false`).
- `getItem` is `readItem(...).then(r => r.item)`: its callers get exactly what they got before (`null` for both kinds). No new export.
- `fetchScopeName` reads `readItem`. On `failed` it records nothing: the name is removed from `names` (so it is neither `pending` nor `answered`), `missing` and `items` are untouched, the scope's `settled` stays false, and the next `readObjectScope` asks it again. No bump on that path: nothing a reader sees has changed, and a bump would re-render straight into another request (a retry loop paced by the failures). No timer, no retry of its own.
- A not-found answer and a found answer record exactly what they did before.

### Measured first: the two producers do tell the cases apart
- SDK path (`@objectstack/client` at the pin `2c9bf94`, `meta.getItem` then the shared `fetch`): every non-ok response throws an `Error` with `httpStatus` and the ADR-0112 `code`; a network failure throws the transport's `TypeError`.
- Preview path (`MetadataClient.get`): a 404 resolves `null`; any other non-ok throws.
- So the split is structural (the declared `code`, or a resolved empty answer), never message text. A 404 carrying no declared code reads as a failed read, as `isMetaItemAbsentError`'s own contract says.

## Tests
- New `packages/app-shell/src/providers/__tests__/MetadataProvider.scopeReadFailure-13009.test.tsx` (8 tests): (a) a 503, a network `TypeError` and a code-less 404 each leave the name out of `missing`, `settled` false, `useObjectPresence` = `{ presence: 'unknown', settled: false }`; the failure alone asks nothing more (count stable over 150ms), and the next read asks again and settles `present`. (b) CONTROL: thrown `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` and a resolved empty read record `missing` and read `absent`; a found answer records the item and reads `present`; `getItem` still answers `null` to its callers for both kinds.
- Fixture triage (respelled, not rewritten): five existing by-name doubles answered "not found" with a bare `Error('404')` or `{ status: 404 }`, a shape no producer throws. Under the new split they read as failed reads, and the tests that assert `missing` / `absent` went red. Each now rejects with the client's not-found shape `{ httpStatus: 404, code: 'RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND' }`: `MetadataProvider.namesOnlyScope-12980`, `MetadataProvider.objectScope-12811`, `packagelessChromeScope-12980`, `AppContent.objectScope-12811`, `AppContent.pageRouteObjects-12980`. The last two are in `console/__tests__`, outside the claim's declared surface. They are named here because the ruling forces the respelling.
- Family run (22 files: every test file under `packages/app-shell/src` named for or mentioning MetadataProvider / objectScope / namesOnlyScope / useObjectPresence / objectPresence / readObjectScope / packagelessChromeScope / getItem, plus the two by-name `AppContent` page-scope suites): `Test Files 22 passed (22)`, `Tests 117 passed (117)` at `d7f1e8b9df`. Before the respelling, the same set read 6 failed files / 8 failed tests.
- The full `packages/app-shell/` directory is declared to CI (not run locally, by the dispatch's lock rule).

## Ablation (one-shot, restored)
`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack) on `MetadataProvider.tsx`: anchor `if (failed) {` became `if (false && failed) {`, so failures are recorded as missing again. Anchor 1 to 0, blob `9d5a5f6743fc` to `e245f2361e64`. Result: all 4 (a) tests red, all 4 controls green. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap: blob after restore = HEAD blob `9d5a5f6743fc3d6713db7838e76b233ecca708f9`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates (at `d7f1e8b9df`)
- Closure build `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: exit 0. `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; the test config lists the new and edited test files): exit 0.
- `eslint` on the 7 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 0 errors (69 warnings, all pre-existing kinds; `MetadataProvider.tsx` 62 against 63 at base). Narrowed: type-aware linting is not configured in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.
- Exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:icon-record-names`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:control-bytes`, `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`.

## Acceptance notes
- In this scope a failed read leaves `settled` false, as ruled. So a consumer that waits for `settled` (the bell) waits until a later read gets an answer. The whole-registry path reads an `error` as settled with presence `unknown`. Under a persistent outage the two paths therefore differ: here the read is held back, there it is performed. The gate never closes on either path.
- A failed name is asked again on the next `readObjectScope` call that reaches it. Any re-render of a reader counts, so under a lasting outage a chrome that re-renders often asks at most once per render, with in-flight requests deduplicated. There is no self-sustaining loop (pinned).
- Noted, not filed: `extractItem` hands back a by-name answer that carries no `item` member as the item itself. objectui#9262 measured that item-less 200 envelope for the `app` type on a real server. If the `object` route answers the same way, a by-name read of a nonexistent object would record the envelope as a found object. Not measured for `object`; no reach. Carrier: none.
- Noted: four more by-name doubles still reject with a bare `Error('404')` (`pageObjectReads-12980`, `InterfaceListPage.packageScope-12980`, `appObjectScope-12811`, `AppContent.pageScopeArms-12980`). Their assertions don't depend on what a not-found records (green before and after), so I left them alone.
